title: Deep learning detects microsatellite instability in colorectal tumours from H&E slides
summary: A deep learning detector was trained on H&E slides from 8,836 colorectal tumours in the MSIDETECT consortium to identify microsatellite instability or mismatch-repair deficiency. Cross-validation (n = 6,406) gave a mean AUROC of 0.92, and performance in an external cohort of 771 specimens was reported at 0.95 to 0.96. The data are retrospective.
ai_technology: Deep-learning detector for MSI/dMMR on H&E whole-slide images
organization: RWTH Aachen University Hospital; Maastricht University Medical Center

evidence.tested: AUROC and AUPRC for MSI/dMMR detection by cross-validation and in an external multi-site cohort.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective data; clinical use and effect on treatment decisions not shown; full text not reviewed.
